messages:
sam.sre: alerting on-call 11: KMS API errors in us-west-2 causing service startup failures. seeing signing errors and KMS timeouts during pod init. paging @lee.sre :rotating_light:
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED  ID=INC-2026-409  Severity=P2  Owner=@sam.sre
sam.sre: quick snapshot: multiple deployments hitting KMS GetPublicKey/Decrypt timeouts ~11:03-11:08 UTC. auto-retries exhausting; some autoscaled pods are stuck in CrashLoopBackOff because init container can't complete signing handshake.
lee.sre: logs?
sam.sre: paste from one init log:
```
init: calling kms:Decrypt arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:... requestId=null
ERROR: request timeout after 30s
retrying (2/3)
init: kms:Decrypt failed: 504 Gateway Timeout
init: aborting
```
maria.infra: confirming CloudWatch -> KMSClient Latency p95 jumped to ~8-12s and API 5xx increased at 11:02 UTC. only affects us-west-2. replication/replicas in other regions unaffected.
tess.platform: impact assessment: public APIs currently OK, but new instance provisioning and jobs that need signing keys fail. customers on-boarding in us-west-2 could see delays. labeling affected feature-flags: onboarding.flow and instance.bootstrap.
product-bot: Notifying product watchers: queued a short note to customers in affected orgs.
sam.sre: immediate mitigations I'm pushing: 1) bump SDK init timeout and retries from 30s/3 -> 90s/6 for init path only; 2) enable local-key-cache fallback for codepaths that can accept cached wrapping keys; 3) reduce parallel init concurrency to 1 per node.
lee.sre: agree. also set KMS client to return a clear error code for upstream so circuit-breakers trip faster.
maria.infra: I'll gate new deployments in us-west-2 and spin up extra capacity in us-east-1 as warm standby for services that can failover. running commands now:
```
aws kms list-keys --region us-east-1
kubectl -n core scale deploy secret-fetcher --replicas=3
```
tess.platform: don't rotate or rekey anything. that could make cached keys invalid.
sam.sre: opened AWS support ticket 10293847 — they acknowledged a regional service disruption and are investigating increased latency.
aws-support-bot: AWS Support: Case 10293847 acknowledged. Collecting traces. Please provide example request IDs.
sam.sre: adding request IDs from logs and enabling extended KMS client traces for 15m. we'll capture X-Amzn-RequestId.
lee.sre: runbook note: if KMS doesn't recover in 45m, we will initiate controlled failover for critical services only: create replicated key in us-east-1 and change KMS_REGION for critical pods. approval required from infra lead.
maria.infra: prepping terraform snippet for key replication but won't apply without sign-off.
ops-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF scheduled: @sam.sre -> @lee.sre at 11:30 UTC.
sam.sre: rolling changes to staging: init succeeded with cache fallback. sample log:
```
init: kms request timeout
using cached-wrapping-key -> success
startup complete
```
tess.platform: customer comms draft ready. recommending "temporary provisioning delays" language, no data exposure.
lee.sre: taking over monitoring. I'm increasing visibility: added KMS client metric dashboard panel and short retention trace to S3 for debugging. also enabling a short 1min alert for any public 5xx > 0.5%.
maria.infra: note: some infra jobs that run at startup will still retry and cause backpressure on KMS. recommend queueing these jobs until stable.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE  INC-2026-409  status: investigating  assigned=@lee.sre
sam.sre: handoff notes posted to incident channel and attached runbook pointers. leaving runbook snippets: avoid KMS admin ops except read/replicate; do not rotate keys; document any region changes in incident log.
lee.sre: received. next steps: 1) monitor AWS updates and our logs for request IDs; 2) limit new inits; 3) if AWS doesn't fix within window, coordinate with infra to perform region-targeted migration for critical services only. escalate to P1 if customer-facing 5xx > 1% sustained 5m.
product-bot: product notified customers at 11:14 UTC. waiting for SRE confirm to send broader status page update.
aws-support-bot: AWS Support: We see elevated latencies in KMS in us-west-2 due to internal throttling. Mitigation in progress.
maria.infra: tracking downstream: secret-manager, signup service, and edge-auth connector are the most impacted. tagging those for constrained deployment.
ops-bot: HANDOFF COMPLETE  new_oncall=@lee.sre  handoff_ts=1781234700
lee.sre: taking over. will update this thread with any changes. closing when services healthy for 30m and AWS confirms resolved.
